pre_call_budget_accounting_clarification.scope: Reference-only protocol clarification before any live reference calls; prompted by controller semantics review, not observed reference outcomes. No frozen Nemotron code, prompts, methods, tasks or budgets changed.
pre_call_budget_accounting_clarification.task_deadline: 180s is the complete task budget including transport/startup and verification. A positively dispatched single-call attempt reaching a controlled deadline, without observed transport/controller/protocol faults, remains in the denominator as a budget-exhausted attempt. Keep verifier-confirmed success if already observed by the frozen controller; otherwise unsolved within budget.
pre_call_budget_accounting_clarification.unknowns: Preserve partial traces, incomplete call/usage and missing infrastructure counts as unknown, never fabricate zero or classify an unfinished request as a proven infrastructure failure. Provider cancellation and residual server cost after a killed client are unmeasured; no global cost/throughput claim.
pre_call_budget_accounting_clarification.output_budget: 8192 output-token cap remains unchanged. A completed length finish or parser/test failure is an observed quality/output-budget outcome, not infrastructure; an actually verified solution remains valid. No automatic repair or extra model call.
pre_call_budget_accounting_clarification.operational_halts: Observed transport/controller/protocol or grader-infrastructure faults still halt the cohort. A deadline during an active coding grade retains its budget outcome but halts for exact-owner cleanup review before reusing any grader; do not continue blindly.
pre_call_budget_accounting_clarification.dispatch_validation: Exactly one trace request_start, matching completed request IDs/counts, and a controller-marked deadline with expected termination exit are required. A missing dispatch, arbitrary crash or ambiguous failed transport is not admitted as a clean budget result.
pre_call_budget_accounting_clarification.portable_context: Local Opus preflight is optional contextual evidence: presence flag and SHA256 or null are recorded. Its absence neither invents auth/model proof nor changes the strict actual-response model/provider check.
